summary: Kay Koppedrayer is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She earned a BA from McGill University and an MA from McMaster University, and retired from Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2005).

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu, working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as headmaster at Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and lecturer at the University of Calcutta (1920).

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed early graduate studies at Kyushu University (-1992). He taught as a lecturer at the University of Miyazaki (~1954–1968) and became professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1968–1995).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947), a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, earned his degrees including a doctorate from Waseda University. He held positions at Tokushima University (1979) and the National Institute of Japanese Literature (1984), retiring from Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and is a fellow at the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University, working in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1982–1990) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013).

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University, earning a DSc. Active in Tibetology and other fields, he was appointed professor of geography in the Graduate School of Letters at Kyoto University (~2009).

Kazuhiko Atsumi (1928–2019) worked in philosophy and other fields, completing his studies at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–2000).

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) studied at Sophia University, Cornell University (PhD under Jay Jasanoff), Kyoto University, and Osaka University. A scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he served at Nagoya City Women's College and Nagoya City University.
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Bukkyo University (attested 2001 and 2013).

Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) completed his doctoral course at Koyasan University, specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held positions at Koyasan University as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointment professor (attested 2026).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).
Kazumi Yoshizaki, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Toyo University and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology (attested 2001).

Kazunobu Matsuda (born 1955) studied at Otani University under Shiro Matsumoto. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Otani University (attested 1985–1989), Bukkyo University (1994, 2009, attested 2022–2024), and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University (PhD under Hajime Sakurabe) and served as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1986–2014).

Kazuo Kano (born 1974) studied at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held appointments at Hamburg, Koyasan University, Kyoto University, and Komazawa University.

Kazuo Matsumura (born 1953) studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976), working in religious studies and Indology. He held academic posts at Tenri University (~1990–1997) and Wako University (~2004).

Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, he held posts at the Institute for Zen Studies (1969) and Komazawa University (1973; professor 1979–2006).

Kazuo Osumi (born 1933) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1964). Active in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he was an assistant professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada (born 1952) studied at Tamagawa University, working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Rissho University.
